subject: ISO / SOC 2: Clarifications on data residency, retention, and deletion controls
messages:
From: Tamara Ellis <tamara@fintrust.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: compliance@fintrust.com
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Questions for SOC2/ISO evidence: retention, residency, deletion

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. As part of our SOC 2 and ISO27001 scoping we need some clarifications on Redwood's retention and deletion controls before we sign off on the integration. Specifically: 

- Where customer data is stored by default (primary region & backups) and how region selection works for Hosted vs Dedicated customers.
- The documented retention schedule for user-generated content, logs, and backups (including retention periods and any tiering).
- Proof/process for deletion: when a customer requests data deletion or after contract termination, what evidence can Redwood provide (audit entries, deletion timestamps, hashes)?
- How legal hold or eDiscovery requests are handled vs automated deletion schedules.
- Whether backups/snapshots are purged on the same schedule or treated differently.
- Support for customer-managed keys (CMK) and whether key deletion effectively renders data unrecoverable for evidence purposes.

If possible, please share the retention matrix and any SOC2/ISO mapping we can attach to our audit file. We can accept an evidence bundle in a secure link. Can you also confirm expected time-to-delete for primary data and for backups once a deletion request is admitted?

We appreciate concise, itemized answers so we can include them in our control testing. If helpful we can do a short follow-up call with our security lead.

Thanks,

Tamara Ellis
Head of Compliance
FinTrust Payments

--

Subject: Re: Questions for SOC2/ISO evidence: retention, residency, deletion

Tamara —

Below are concise, itemized answers to your list, plus where we'll include the supporting artifacts in the evidence bundle. Please let me know if you need deeper logs or specific control IDs called out for your auditor.

1) Data residency (primary & backups)
- Hosted API: primary storage region is selected by customer at project creation. Default for accounts created from our US sign-up flow is us-west-2 (Oregon). Backups and cross-region replication are configurable: by default we take encrypted snapshots and keep a single encrypted cross-region copy in us-east-1 for DR.
- Dedicated/Private: customers can pin workloads to a VPC region or on-prem location; our private control plane can be configured to avoid cross-region replication.
- Evidence: architecture diagram + region mapping spreadsheet (included in redwood_data_retention_matrix_v2.xlsx).

2) Retention schedule (user content, logs, backups)
- User-generated content (short-term inference artifacts): default retention 30 days (used for caching/KV speedups) unless customer sets a different TTL via project settings.
- Customer-stored artifacts (uploads, user-managed files): retention controlled by explicit lifecycle rules; default retention 90 days if not overridden.
- Audit/system logs: retained 365 days in segmented storage for incident investigation; aggregated metrics retained 13 months.
- Backups/snapshots: primary snapshot retention 30 days; longer-term snapshot retention 90 days for customers on enterprise retention policies.
- Evidence: retention matrix (sheet: retention_policies) and sample lifecycle rule JSON (in bundle).

3) Deletion process & proof
- Deletion request flow:
  a) Customer initiates deletion via Console/API -> triggers Job ID and a background workflow in the Data Retention Service.
  b) Job runs to remove active objects, purge caches, and raise deletion events to the audit log.
  c) Backups are scheduled for purge subject to backup retention windows (see #2).
- Proof artifacts we can provide: deletion_job_id, audit log entries (timestamped), object tombstone hashes, and the deletion runbook excerpt.
- For SOC 2 evidence we provide a sample redaction/deletion audit transcript (with redacted PII) and the raw deletion Job IDs that auditors can cross-check.

4) Legal hold / eDiscovery
- Legal holds override automated retention: when a hold is placed, the Data Retention Service marks relevant objects as exempt and they are excluded from purge until hold removal. Holds are logged and require a justified request from the customer via the Console + contact with our compliance team.
- Evidence: legal hold runbook and a sample hold audit trail (included).

5) Backups / snapshots
- Backups are purged according to backup retention windows (see #2). We do not immediately delete backup copies upon a primary deletion request unless the customer explicitly requests accelerated purge and the account does not have a hold.
- For customers requiring accelerated deletion of backups we offer an enterprise option (contract amendment) that can reduce backup retention to 30 days and include a documented purge run.

6) Customer-managed keys (CMK)
- We support KMS integrations for hosted customers: keys can be customer-managed in AWS KMS. If a customer deletes a CMK, it renders ciphertext unrecoverable; we can provide attestation that no plaintext copies remain under Redwood control (subject to backup retention policies).
- Evidence: KMS integration notes + sample key rotation policy excerpt.

References to standards and control mapping:
- SOC 2: relevant CC6/CC7 evidence mapping included in SOC2_Audit_RESPONSE_2025.pdf.
- ISO27001: Annex A controls mapping included in the same PDF.

Artifacts we will attach to the secure folder: redwood_data_retention_matrix_v2.xlsx (matrix + region map), SOC2_Audit_Response_2025.pdf (control mappings & high-level attestations), deletion_runbook_excerpt.txt, sample_deletion_audit.csv (redacted).

If you would like a short demo of a live deletion (on a synthetic dataset) we can run one with you and capture the Job ID and audit trail.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions for SOC2/ISO evidence: retention, residency, deletion

Tamara —

Appreciate the precise asks. Below are concrete, auditable responses we can include in the bundle and also language you can drop into procurement: 

1) Redacted deletion Job audit sample
- Action: we'll provide a redacted CSV capturing one synthetic deletion Job (job_id: JOB-20251117-3344), with timestamps for request, execution start, object tombstones written, and final audit confirmation. This will be uploaded to the secure Drive link I shared.

2) CMK plaintext retention
- Statement (for your auditor): "Redwood Inference does not retain customer plaintext copies outside of the KMS envelope for customer-managed keys. All customer ciphertext stored by Redwood is encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys and plaintext is not persisted in any long-lived systems beyond ephemeral processing buffers; those buffers are cleared per our memory management policy."

3) Sample contractual language for time-to-delete
- Primary data: "Redwood will remove customer primary data from active storage and mark the account for deletion within 30 calendar days following termination or a verified deletion request, excluding any data under legal hold."
- Backups: "Standard backup retention is 90 calendar days; backups will be purged in accordance with the backup retention schedule. Customers may opt-in to an accelerated backup purge (enterprise addendum) which will reduce backup retention to 30 calendar days and include an attested purge report."

4) DocuSign attestation
- We can provide a DocuSign-safe attestation with the above language and Neha's signature. Link to be generated once you confirm final wording.

I attached the retention matrix and the SOC2 mapping PDF to this thread for your immediate review. If you'd like the live demo to capture a Job ID in real-time, Marissa can schedule it for later this week.

Let me know if this hits the mark and I'll have legal/ops prepare the DocuSign attestation.

Best,
Jonas Weber
